required_tuples.rationale: A batch scan of two folder items answers 200 and rescans each of them, so each item takes the title of its edited metadata.json and its sidecar is rewritten to match.
The same batch scan again answers 200, leaves both items' rows and sidecars unchanged and sends no item_updated event for them.
A batch that mixes a file library item with a folder item answers 200, rescans only the folder item and leaves the file item row untouched.
Batch scan answers 401 without a token, 403 for a non-admin, 400 for an empty list and 400 when no id matches an item; rejected requests rescan nothing.

A scan cancelled through the cancel_scan socket event stops before completing: its task finishes with the message "Task canceled by user", the library's lastScan is not moved and fewer than all staged items are added.
Scanning an item rereads its metadata/items/<id>/metadata.json, applies title, authors and series from it, creates the unknown author and series rows and answers {result:"UPDATED"}.
An immediate second scan of an unchanged item answers {result:"UPTODATE"} and leaves the item row and its metadata.json untouched.
A scan applies the chapters array of metadata.json verbatim (ids renumbered from 0, start/end untouched) together with the title while the three audio files keep their stored order and durations.
Scanning a podcast item rereads metadata/items/<id>/metadata.json, applies the podcast keys title, author and genres, answers {result:"UPDATED"} and rewrites the sidecar with the podcast key set.
An anonymous request answers 401, a user without update permission 403, an unknown item 404 and a file library item 500; none changes the item, its sidecar or its author links.

An admin scan answers 200 and, when it completes, moves the library's lastScan strictly forward, stamps lastScanVersion 2.37.2 and persists the configured metadata precedence in extraData while the item rows keep their ids and titles.
A second scan of an unchanged library answers 200, moves lastScan strictly forward again, adds no item and leaves every item's lastScan timestamp unchanged.
A plain scan does not reread a metadata.json stored outside the library tree, so an edit there leaves the item title unchanged while the library records the scan.
A forced scan (?force=1) rescans every item even without file changes, so the same edited metadata.json is applied and the item title becomes the sidecar title.
A scan after a new book folder appears adds exactly one item whose title and author come from the folder names and writes its metadata.json sidecar; the response itself stays 200.
Library scan answers 401 without a token, 403 for a non-admin, 403 for an admin without access to the library and 404 for an unknown library id; no rejected request scans or moves lastScan.

A media update writes metadata/items/<id>/metadata.json with exactly the seventeen book keys, the values of the item document and the book key set (no podcast keys); the file is not one of the item's library files.
Repeating the same media update answers updated false and leaves metadata.json byte-identical, because no change is written again.

A metadata.json edited directly is reread by a scan: the series string "Round Trip Saga #7" becomes series name and sequence, the edited publishedYear and isbn reach the item, and the writer restores the same values in the file.

Clearing fields writes explicit null and empty arrays (not missing keys) into metadata.json, and a following scan still rebuilds the values other sources supply, so the file's null and empty values neither break reading nor erase the item.
When metadata.json cannot be written the media update still answers updated true and the item keeps the new values, while the file on disk keeps its previous content.

With the default precedence the metadata.json of a new item overrides folder and tag sources for every field it supplies, so title, authors, genres and the numeric publishedYear come from the sidecar while the item folder names supply nothing of them.

Changing the library's metadataPrecedence to put absMetadata first forces the next scan to re-evaluate items whose files did not change, so folder names win for title and authors while sidecar-only fields keep their values, and the order is persisted in extraData.lastScanMetadataPrecedence.

A sidecar whose null and empty values are skipped applies its non-empty title and leaves the fields only the sidecar supplied (series, genres, chapters, publishedYear) at their stored values, while authors are re-derived from the folder because folderStructure supplies them.

After one of a three-file book's audio files is deleted, a rescan rebuilds the chapters from the two remaining files: ids 0/1, titles from the title tags and offsets that are the cumulative durations of the files in track order.
A repeat scan of the restored three-file book answers UPTODATE and leaves its three audio files, three chapters and metadata.json unchanged.

Moving a book folder to another author and series keeps the same library item and book id, relinks the book to the new author and series with sequence 2, and deletes the author and series rows left without books.
Moving a single-file item's audio file into a folder keeps the item's identity through the inode fallback: the same item and book id, now a folder item with the moved file as its only audio file.
A metadata.json that is not valid JSON is ignored by the scan: the item answers UPTODATE, keeps its stored metadata and the file is left as it is.

A new item folder whose second audio file cannot be probed still imports with exactly one audio file; the scan completes, records the folder as one item and stores the unusable file without an audio entry.

A new podcast folder imports as one item whose episodes take their titles and dates from the audio tags; a later item scan adds a newly copied episode file and removes an episode whose file was deleted.
Adding a cover.jpg to an item folder that has no cover sets media.coverPath to that file on the next scan, and deleting the file clears coverPath again.

A book that keeps audio but loses its ebook drops ebookFile without becoming missing and regains it when the file returns; a book left with no media file at all is flagged missing by the next scan and recovers when a media file returns.
A book whose audio file carries attached cover art and has no image file in its folder gets that art extracted into the metadata directory and set as the item cover.
A book whose remaining audio file cannot be probed and which has no ebook is flagged missing by the scan, and the flag clears when a probeable file returns.
A new book folder holding one audio file and one epub imports as one item with the probed audio file and the epub as its ebookFile with ebookFormat epub.
A scan that adds twelve books delivers every new item in items_added events of at most ten items each, and no item is delivered twice.

With the default precedence each file source contributes in order: the nfo sets series, genres and publisher, desc.txt/reader.txt set description and narrators, and the later opf overwrites title, authors, description, publisher, language and publishedYear while the fields the opf does not supply keep their nfo/txt values.

A metadataPrecedence array naming an unknown source is accepted and persisted, and a scan ignores that name: only the folder-derived title is applied while the stored series and genres stay, and restoring the default order applies the sidecar again.
When the scanner cannot write metadata.json it still applies and stores the new metadata and the scan answers UPDATED, while the read-only file keeps its previous content.
An item whose only media is an ebook imports with the epub as ebookFile and no audio file, and scanning it again answers UPDATED or UPTODATE while keeping the title stored in its metadata.json.
With the library watcher enabled, a new book folder produces a watcher-scan task that adds the item without a library scan, so libraries.lastScan stays unchanged while the item appears.

Setting autoScanCronExpression to a per-minute schedule makes the server run a library scan by itself: a library-scan task finishes, lastScan moves forward and the newly staged book is imported without any scan request.

One scan of a library root adds a single-file item for a media file in the root, folds CD01/CD02 folders into one item, and ignores dot directories, @eaDir, temporary extensions and folders flagged by a .ignore file.
A media file in the root of a podcast library becomes no item, because root files are filtered out for podcast libraries.
The CD01/CD02 book's two files are ordered by disc number and index 1/2, carry the probed mp3 fields, and produce two chapters whose offsets are the cumulative durations in that order.
Renaming an item folder in place keeps the same item and book ids and the folder inode, updates path and relPath, and keeps the title stored in the item's metadata.json.

A forced scan applies the library's persisted metadataPrecedence order and re-persists it unchanged in extraData, so absMetadata first lets the folder title win while the stored sidecar values remain for the other fields.
A scan that adds a book writes metadata/items/<id>/metadata.json only (the item folder gets none), and the written file carries the item's values without becoming one of the item's library files.

A scan that adds a book sends one items_added array holding the expanded item to the root and listener sockets and to no socket of a user restricted to another library or of an unauthenticated client.
A scan after an item folder disappears reports one missing, zero added and zero updated, flags the row missing, and a second scan reports the same missing count again instead of clearing it.
Deleting every episode file of a podcast whose folder still exists leaves the podcast item not missing and reports zero missing, and the episodes stay stored.

A scan of a library whose folder path no longer exists adds nothing, reports every item missing, flags all rows missing and still records the completed scan; a scan after the folder returns clears the flags.
A folder whose only audio file cannot be probed becomes no library item and the scan still completes, while the other items of the library keep their rows.

not_applicable.reason: confirmed: batchScan reads only req.body.libraryItemIds and calls LibraryItemScanner.scanLibraryItem for every non-file id; there is no force, hard or override query/body parameter (server/controllers/LibraryItemController.js:820-856).

confirmed: scan() checks isAdminOrUp and isFile and then calls LibraryItemScanner.scanLibraryItem; it reads no query or body parameter and every call rescans the item (server/controllers/LibraryItemController.js:860-877).

confirmed: LibraryItem.saveMetadataFile and BookScanner.saveMetadataFile write the sidecar only after an accepted media change or a scan that detected changes; neither has a force/override mode (server/models/LibraryItem.js:614-711, server/scanner/BookScanner.js:825-901).

open_findings: scan-precedence-timeline/sub-scanner-watcher: no scenario pins the known quirk that BookScanner.js:425-429 re-saves the libraryItem instances LibraryScanner loaded at the start of the scan, so a live write to the same row during the scan can be overwritten; a Go rewrite that preserves the live write passes while upstream loses it. Add a scenario that starts a scan, writes an affected item field through a live route mid-scan, and asserts the upstream outcome, or record the quirk as an explicit exception in the record.

sub-scanner-watcher: the contract names 'chunked items_added/items_updated events', but no scenario asserts items_updated at all; only items_added is covered (items-added-events-are-chunked, scan-events-filter-by-library-access). Add a library scan that updates ten or more items and asserts items_updated chunk size, no duplicate delivery and the same audience filter (server/scanner/LibraryScanner.js:224-240).

route-r038: library-scan-without-force-skips-unread-sidecar sends no force parameter. The web client always sends ?force=0 for a plain scan (client/store/libraries.js:76) and upstream compares req.query.force === '1' (server/controllers/LibraryController.js:1272), so a server that treats any present value as force passes. Request ?force=0 and assert the sidecar is still skipped.

route-r038: library-scan-records-completion and library-scan-repeat-is-stable compare only item titles, while INV-R038-RESPONSE-001 requires the item ids to stay unchanged and the repeat Claim says every item's lastScan stays unchanged (only the first item is checked). Capture relPath->id and each item's lastScan before the scan and compare after.

scan-precedence-timeline/sub-scanner-watcher: audio-disc-order-and-chapters verifies the chapter offsets only as lower bounds (Start >= expected-delta, End >= cumulative), so a server returning e.g. (0,20),(20,20) for two 10 s files passes. Assert chapter.Start and chapter.End equal the cumulative duration within 1e-6, as chapters-removal-rebuilds-offsets does.

sub-scanner-watcher: ebook-only-item-scans-with-ebook-metadata never asserts an ebook-derived value. The staged folder is 'Ebook Author/Ebook Only Item' but the epub's title/creator are 'Ebook Only'/'Ada Example', so a server that ignores ebook metadata entirely (folder title survives before and after) passes. Assert the literal title/author after the import and after the rescan.

route-r062: item-scan-applies-podcast-sidecar writes author 'Sidecar Host' but never asserts it on the item or the rewritten sidecar, and the 'exact canonical podcast key set' the invariant requires is not pinned (only title, podcastType, genres and the absence of authors/chapters/abridged are checked), so a scanner dropping the author or a writer omitting feedURL/imageURL/itunes*/releaseDate/asin/language passes. Assert the applied author and all fifteen podcast keys.

scan-precedence-timeline: precedence-absent-and-empty-keep-values never writes an empty tags array, so the tags skip branch of AbsMetadataFileScanner.js:38 that INV-SCAN-PRECEDENCE-ABSENT-001 names is unproven; add "tags": [] to the empty sidecar and assert the stored tags survive.

format-metadata-json: wantSidecarMatchesItem compares every scalar except subtitle, so metadata-json-written-by-media-update passes a writer that emits "subtitle": null while the item's subtitle is 'Format Subtitle' (INV-FORMAT-METADATA-JSON requires the current values). Compare the stored subtitle with the item metadata.

sub-scanner-watcher: book-with-unprobeable-audio-is-missing claims the missing flag clears when a probeable file returns, but the deferred restore only requires the scan result UPDATED; it never asserts isMissing is false. Assert the cleared flag after the restore scan.

route-r062: item-scan-applies-edited-sidecar claims it 'creates the unknown author and series rows', but 'Long Saga' already exists in the fixture and the scenario asserts it is not duplicated; only the author row is created. Either use an unknown series and assert the new row and sequence, or narrow the Claim to linking the existing series.

sub-scanner-watcher: the requirement records are incomplete: book-with-unprobeable-audio-is-missing is not listed under INV-SCAN-MISSING-001 and items-added-events-are-chunked is not listed under INV-SCAN-EVENTS-001 in cap-sub-scanner-watcher.json, although both scenarios declare those invariants. Add the two run_test.go references to the matching invariant tests lists.
